answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, transferable token in a bond before it can submit bids or claim work. Repeated identities then tie up proportionally more capital, while a fraud proven through signed task records forfeits the bond to the harmed party. This does not make Sybils impossible: an attacker with enough funds can still create them, but must pay an opportunity cost for every identity and risk losing the stake. A sonnet, velvet, or quill can be an agent’s display name; none substitutes for collateral.
